findings.text: the check at :2915 is not followed by a second reading of the discard record, and the pointer it guards carries `"pid": None` (published at :2753/2856-2867) until `_mutate_pointer` attaches the spawned pid at :2956; a discard landing in that span is therefore not refused by `promotion.discard` (record_process_alive answers None for a record naming no process, reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:24-25), it removes the pointer, and the rollback that follows destroys the run directory holding the only discard record, leaving a spawned worker that neither a pointer nor a discard record names — the same defect the node repairs, one fork later, and untested.

the recorded residual window states that a discard landing after the check still arrives against a live run and is refused by `discard`'s own liveness test; for an unplaced run the published pointer carries no pid, so `record_process_alive` returns None and the discard proceeds rather than being refused, which makes the paragraph's account of the remaining window the opposite of what the path does.

`baseline_suite` and `after_suite` are written as Python set literals (`{"revision", "0ab156b37...", ...}`), so `reports._parse_suite_observation` keeps each as a raw string and every field reads None; at promotion `_head_suite_failure_ids` then answers None and `_baseline_suite_failure_ids` answers `set()`, so the negative-control comparator degrades to `reference_ids = set()` and any red log is admitted as an added failure — the node's own control passes for a reason that is not a comparison.

the `# module.__file__:` header carries an AttributeError traceback (`'function' object has no attribute '__file__'`) rather than a module path, so the log names no path for the module under test and the header reads as a measurement it did not make.

the importer arms cover the 31 test files that reference a function on the changed path rather than every test file that imports reckon/crew/dispatch.py or reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py as the done_when requires; the narrowing is disclosed and principled (the 321-file population hit a 700 s cap at ~43% with EXIT=124), but a test that reaches `dispatch`'s spawn path without naming those functions is not covered.
